categories.main_business_segments: DXC operates through two primary segments: Global Business Services (GBS) and Global Infrastructure Services (GIS). GBS focuses on analytics and engineering, applications, and insurance software and business process services. GIS provides security, cloud infrastructure and IT outsourcing, and modern workplace solutions. These segments deliver a broad range of IT services to modernize and manage customers' IT estates.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: DXC leverages advanced technologies such as cloud computing (hybrid and multicloud orchestration), cybersecurity (including Zero Trust strategies), data analytics, automation, software engineering, and proprietary modular insurance platforms. The company utilizes proven methodologies, intelligent automation, and a global delivery model, including significant offshore capabilities, to deliver mission-critical IT services and solutions.
categories.primary_customers_markets: DXC serves a diverse customer base, including approximately half of the Fortune 500, across multiple industries such as insurance, banking, healthcare, manufacturing, and the public sector. Its offerings are tailored to both commercial enterprises of all sizes and public sector organizations, with no single customer accounting for more than 10% of revenue.
categories.geographic_coverage: DXC operates in approximately 70 countries, with significant revenue generated in the United States, United Kingdom, other European countries, Australia, and other international markets. About 70% of its revenues are derived from outside the U.S., reflecting a broad global footprint.
categories.supply_chain_position: DXC operates as a downstream IT services provider, delivering end-to-end solutions directly to enterprise and public sector clients. The company is positioned at the customer-facing end of the IT services supply chain, integrating and managing technology from various hardware, software, and cloud partners.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: DXC's strategic priorities center on customer-centric transformation, cost optimization, portfolio rationalization, and revenue stabilization. The company invests in innovation areas such as cloud migration, digital transformation, cybersecurity, data-driven sustainability, and modern workplace solutions, while divesting non-core assets to focus on its six differentiated offerings.
categories.revenue_model: DXC generates revenue primarily through long-term service contracts, including time and materials, unit-price, and fixed-price agreements, as well as software licensing, business process outsourcing, and managed services. Revenue is recognized over time as services are delivered, with some contracts including upfront fees and variable consideration.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: DXC competes in a highly competitive global IT services market against large multinational firms (such as Accenture, IBM, and Tata Consultancy Services), specialized service providers, offshore firms (notably from India), and in-house IT departments. The company positions itself as a leader in mission-critical IT services with deep expertise in modernization and transformation.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: For fiscal year 2023, DXC reported revenues of $14.4 billion, down 11.3% from the prior year, reflecting foreign exchange headwinds, divestitures, and organic revenue decline. The company is large in scale but has experienced revenue contraction in recent years, with ongoing efforts to stabilize and return to growth through transformation initiatives.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: DXC emphasizes its ability to deliver mission-critical IT services that modernize operations, drive innovation, and reduce risk for global enterprises. Its differentiation lies in its comprehensive service portfolio, global delivery capability, deep industry expertise, and focus on tailored, scalable solutions that enable clients to achieve digital transformation and operational excellence.
